content: Pyrantel pamoate is an anthelmintic medication approved by the FDA for the treatment of pinworm infections. Common side effects associated with its use include diarrhea, nausea, vomiting, dizziness, headache, and drowsiness. Adult Indications and Dosage FDA-Labeled Indications and Dosage (Adults): Pyrantel pamoate suspension is used to treat pinworm infections. The dosage is weight-based: 63–87 lbs: 5 mL 88–112 lbs: 10 mL 113–137 lbs: 15 mL 138–162 lbs: 20 mL 163–187 lbs: 25 mL 188 lbs and above: 30 mL Off-Label Use and Dosage (Adults): Ascariasis: A single dose of 11 mg/kg. Moniliformis infection: 11 mg/kg as a single dose, repeated twice at two-week intervals. Uncinaria infection: 11 mg/kg/day for three days. Trichostrongyliasis: 11 mg/kg (maximum dose: 1 gram). Pediatric Indications and Dosage FDA-Labeled Indications and Dosage (Pediatrics): Pyrantel pamoate suspension is used for treating pinworm infections in children aged 2 to 12 years. Dosage is weight-based: Less than 25 lbs (11 kg) or under 2 years old: Do not use unless directed by a physician. 25–37 lbs: 2.5 mL 38–62 lbs: 5 mL 63–87 lbs: 10 mL 88–112 lbs: 15 mL 113–137 lbs: 20 mL 138–162 lbs: 25 mL 163–187 lbs: 30 mL 188 lbs and above: 35 mL Off-Label Use and Dosage (Pediatrics): Ascariasis: A single dose of 11 mg/kg. Moniliformis infection: 11 mg/kg as a single dose, repeated twice at two-week intervals. Uncinaria infection: 11 mg/kg/day for three days. Trichostrongyliasis: 11 mg/kg (maximum dose: 1 gram). Contraindications Pyrantel pamoate is contraindicated in pregnant individuals and those with liver disease. Warnings Keep this medication out of reach of children. In the event of accidental overdose, seek professional assistance or contact a Poison Control Center immediately. Adverse Reactions Clinical Trials Experience: Abdominal cramps, nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, headache, and dizziness have been reported. Postmarketing Experience: Limited information is available regarding postmarketing data for pyrantel pamoate. Drug Interactions There is limited information available regarding drug interactions with pyrantel pamoate. Use in Specific Populations Pregnancy: Classified as Category C by the FDA and Category B2 by Australian guidelines. There is no specific guidance on its use during pregnancy. Labor and Delivery: No FDA guidance is available for its use during labor and delivery. Nursing Mothers: No FDA guidance is available for its use in breastfeeding women. Pediatric Use: No specific FDA guidance is available for pediatric use beyond labeled indications. Geriatric Use: No specific FDA guidance is available for use in elderly populations. Gender, Race, Renal Impairment, Hepatic Impairment, and Immunocompromised Patients: No specific FDA guidance is available for these populations. Administration and Monitoring Administration: Pyrantel pamoate is administered orally. Monitoring: Limited information is available regarding monitoring requirements for this medication. Overdosage Limited information is available regarding overdose. In case of suspected overdose, contact the National Poison Help hotline (1-800-222-1222) immediately. Pharmacology Mechanism of Action: Limited information is available in the drug label. Structure, Pharmacodynamics, and Pharmacokinetics: Limited information is available in the drug label. Nonclinical Toxicology: Limited information is available in the drug label. Clinical Studies Limited information is available regarding clinical studies for pyrantel pamoate. How Supplied Pyrantel pamoate suspension is available in 32 fl. oz. (946 mL) bottles. Storage Store at 20°–25°C (68°–77°F). Patient Counseling Information Limited information is available regarding patient counseling for pyrantel pamoate. Precautions with Alcohol The interaction between alcohol and pyrantel pamoate has not been established. Consult your doctor regarding the effects of alcohol consumption while taking this medication. Brand Names Pyrantel pamoate is marketed under the brand names Ascarel, Pamix, and Pin-X. Look-Alike Drug Names Limited information is available regarding look-alike drug names for pyrantel pamoate.
